children: Falling oil prices are helping U.S. tech stocks stay buoyant Tuesday.

The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite Index rose modestly in late trading, poised for a second straight record high. The Dow industrials slipped and the S&P 500 traded near flat. Brent crude futures edged lower, falling to roughly $100 a barrel after encouraging news about oil exports from the Middle East.

Saudi Arabia is running tests on its East-West pipeline and could restart flows as early as this week. The pipeline, a crucial route circumventing Hormuz, was recently closed after drone attacks. Japan's Kyodo News Agency separately reported that Iran has proposed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. lifts its blockade.

President Trump addressed world leaders this morning at the United Nations General Assembly in New York, arguing that his overseas interventions had made the world safer. Investors are also eyeing whether a meeting between Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian will materialize after Trump said over the weekend that he was "probably" open to it.

Global government bond yields are following oil prices lower. The 10-year yield is trading around 4.95%. Stocks tied to the artificial-intelligence trade are mixed after an enthusiastic reception for Meta's new AI agent lifted the sector Monday.
